question: How many countries participated in the first Asian Games held in 1951?
solution:
The correct answer is __**11**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **11 countries** participated in the first Asian Games held in 1951.
 
• The first Asian Games were hosted by **New Delhi, India** from March 4 to March 11, 1951.
 
• The participating countries were Afghanistan, Burma (Myanmar), Ceylon (Sri Lanka), India, Indonesia, Iran, Japan, Nepal, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand.
 
• The Asian Games, also known as Asiad, are a multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from all over Asia.
 
• The event is organized by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) and is recognized by the International Olympic Committee (IOC).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The idea of the Asian Games was initiated by India's first Prime Minister, **Jawaharlal Nehru**, and the Asian Games Federation was formed to organize the games.
 
• The first Asian Games featured six sports: athletics, aquatics (swimming, diving, water polo), basketball, cycling, football, and weightlifting.
 
• Since the inaugural event in 1951, the Asian Games have grown significantly in size and scope, with more countries and sports being added over the years.
 
• The Asian Games are considered the second-largest multi-sport event after the Olympic Games.
